data.content_ref: inline:The target's defense relies on 'verisimilitude' (proximity to truth) as the justification for preferring better-corroborated theories, but this smuggles in induction because Popper's own formal definition of verisimilitude was refuted by Tichý and Miller, leaving no non-inductive logical basis to claim one theory is 'closer to truth' than another based solely on past survival.
